contracts.title: Greener Tourism
contracts.description:
By utilising some of the remaining Additional Restrictions Grant (ARG) funding provided by central Government, West Lancashire Borough Council would like to provide some wider business support opportunities.
In line with the Vision and Priorities (Support businesses to adapt and prosper & Become a Greener West Lancashire), we would like to support our local businesses achieve a 'greener' industry standard that demonstrates environmental responsibility and sustainable operation and are seeking an external provider to deliver this initiative.
This would be a contract for a service delivered to local businesses which enables local businesses in the retail, hospitality, and leisure sectors to improve sustainability and environmental responsibility and in doing so, achieve an industry standard accreditation.

Key Specifications
• Provider can provide industry standard accreditation to SMEs throughout West Lancashire across various sectors (Accommodation, Hospitality, Leisure, Retail & Tourism)
• Provider will deliver training, support and the final accreditation to approx. 100 businesses
• The project can be delivered between April 2022 and March 2023, with the support in promotion by West Lancashire Borough Council
• Previous experience of delivering similar accreditation initiatives on behalf of a Local Authority

contracts.title: Ecology Advisory Services
contracts.description:
For Further information and Tender documents please visit https://www.the-chest.org.uk/.                                                           
West Lancashire is a largely rural authority with some of the most valuable habitats for a wide range of protected species, many of which are designated as important international and national habitats. As part of its development management function the Council is keen to ensure that the impacts of development on protected sites and species are recognised and mitigated and that biodiversity is enhanced. The Council seeks expert advice from Ecological Consultancies to help achieve this through an Ecological Development Advice Service.

West Lancashire Borough Council receives a diverse mix of planning applications from rural barn conversions to major residential development schemes, which have wide-ranging ecological impacts. Over the last 3 years, the Council has on average made 55 consultation requests per annum to our current ecological provider and our current contract provides for 1000 hours of ecology service officer time. West Lancashire Borough Council supports and contributes to the maintenance of the Lancashire Environmental Records network, hosted by Lancashire County Council and the Council's ecological consultants will have access to this record for development management purposes.

contracts.title: West Lancashire Borough Council - Community grants - Infrastructure
contracts.description:
Background

Following a review of its support to voluntary organisations, the Council is supporting the provision of infrastructure support for voluntary, community and faith sector organisations (VCFS) within the Borough through the provision of a Grant.  The Grant will commence from 1 April 2020 for a maximum 3 year period, subject to annual budget processes and satisfactory progress in meeting the outcomes and the indicative measures by the successful Bidder.

Outcomes

Infrastructure support has been identified as an area of critical need in order to help secure the future capacity of the sector to deliver services in the Borough.  The Council's investment is expected to help to deliver the following outcomes:-
•	The resilience of the VCFS in the Borough is improved
•	VCFS organisations in the Borough working together to deliver services and share costs and resources
•	Volunteer recruitment, placement and retention
•	To engage with and promote the West Lancashire employability, health and wellbeing programmes. 


Tender documents are available via 'The Chest' https://www.the-chest.org.uk   Bidders should visit the 'Current opportunities' page and then click on the drop down menu for 'West Lancashire Borough Council' to access the tender opportunity.

Tenders must be submitted by 9/12/2019 2.00pm via https://the-chest.org.uk.

Clarifications in relation to this requirement must be submitted via the messaging system within 'The Chest' https://www.the-chest.org.uk by 03/12/19 2.00pm.

contracts.description:
West Lancashire Borough Council (the Council) is seeking to engage an experienced and suitably qualified Contractor to provide the provision a new cycle path on an existing footpath on land between Ormskirk bus and rail station approximately 215m in length.  The Council wants to upgrade the existing footpath to create a shared use cycle way/footpath to provide improved access for pedestrians and cyclists between the existing train station and bus station.  This cycle path/footpath will ultimately link to a wider cycle network.

2.	Relocating and upgrading existing lighting columns as identified on plans 
3.	Relaying of a new Styrene Butadiene Rubber/Aggregate surface (SBRA) or similar alternative surface material. 
4.	On site treatment/management of Japanese Knotweed as identified in the Japanese Knotweed Management Plan. 
5.	Widening of the path at specified locations including the introduction of retaining gabion walls features
6.	Introduction of new bollards and signage  
7.	Introduction of a new DDA compliant handrail to extend the full length of the path

The project is required to commence before 1st November 2019 and be completed 24th December 2019.

contracts.title: West Lancashire Borough Council - Expression of Interest for Food insecurity project
contracts.description:
The health consequences of household food insecurity are long term, severe and expensive. We are looking to commission an organisation to analyse and measure food insecurity in West Lancashire so that we can be clear about who is affected and can target policy and resources on prevention.

The scope of the brief will be as follows; 

•	To establish a better understanding of who is using food banks in the Borough and to provide insight into potential gaps in access to them or gaps in accessing sufficient welfare support.

•	To evaluate the socio demographic and household characteristics of households in the borough subject to food insecurity creating a clear understanding of the local picture.
•	To understand the severity and chronicity of household food insecurity and how often people are receiving assistance from food banks and other supporting agencies 
•	To establish the economic status of those facing insecurity
•	Establish and asses the current support and provision already available in the Borough to address the issues.
•	To consider the health implications of those living with food insecurity.

In addition the following will need to be considered,

•	The steps the Borough can take to prevent food inequality.
•	How the Borough can make the best use of the services and approaches already available and respond more effectively.  This will include looking at a range of services in the local area.
•	Identify opportunities for communities across the borough to grow their own food, either through the Community Food Growing network, West Lancashire Allotment Federation, primary and secondary schools.
•	How community centres and voluntary organisations can support the local Birchwood Junk Food Cafe model and divert supermarket waste food from landfill.

contracts.description:
West Lancashire Borough Council is seeking expressions of interest from organisations to take over and run the Chapel Gallery on a commercial basis. However, the vision for the Gallery is that it retains an arts and cultural focus with exhibitions, performances, films and other cultural activities that draw people into the town and contribute to the economic and social activity of Ormskirk.

The Chapel Gallery plays a pivotal role as Ormskirk's creative and cultural hub providing new and compelling reasons for people to visit the town centre. The Council would expect a new operator to introduce new activities that would contribute positively to the town centre with complementary uses that would increasing footfall and vibrancy within the town and the Gallery itself.

As well as exhibitions, a regular arts club is held along with workshops, talks and summer holiday clubs. Further details can be provided to interested parties. Where practicable it is envisaged that the new operator will continue with these bookings. 

The Gallery hosts a number of events including the Lancashire Open in the summer and other exhibitions as well as supporting town centre events such as the annual Christmas Lights Switch on, Gingerbread Festival and Motorfest.

contracts.title: Provision of Vehicles and Vehicle Maintenance Services - Soft Market Test
contracts.description:
West Lancashire Borough Council is keen to explore options for the future provision and maintenance of the Council's vehicle fleet (currently 58 vehicles including a number of refuse collection vehicles).  The Council requires a professionally operated service that can provide an excellent vehicle management service.
The Council provides a wide range of frontline services including street cleansing, grounds maintenance, the collection of refuse and recycling material. In continuing to provide these services in an efficient, effective manner a competent vehicle management service is essential.
The Council plans to conduct a procurement exercise to appoint a contractor to provide vehicles and deliver the maintenance work associated to those vehicles from September 2020. The proposed contract period is five years plus up to three additional years. The works involved will cover both planned and also responsive repairs.
The purpose of this Soft Market Test exercise is to allow interested organisations with appropriate experience to outline their views and provide information by completing a short questionnaire, with no commitment to themselves or to the Council. The Council will use this feedback to inform the development of the tender specification, gauge the level of interest from the market to establish that there are sufficient potential partners to ensure that a genuine competition is likely within a future procurement process, and to ensure that the proposed procurement programme is viable.

Images arrive at the suite via a mixture of different transmission methods. These are • The Council's private fibre digital network. • Silvernet Wireless Transmission • Analogue BT RS1000 circuits • BT EPS9 local exchange circuits • Fibre to the Cabinet (VPN), and • ADSL (VPN) Bidders will be required to proactively and reactively maintain cameras, the suite, transmission equipment and supporting technical equipment to ensure that the system operates with minimal "downtime", within the relevant legislation and best practice, as determined by applying British or equivalent European Standards, ACPO, ICO, Surveillance Camera Commissioner and UK Home Office Guidance.

West Lancashire Borough Council is seeking to appoint a development partner to design and build a town centre mixed use scheme including the provision of a new, fit for purpose, modern, bus station facility, and uses that contribute to the wider regeneration of Ormskirk Town Centre.  The scheme must provide:

•             At least 900sqm of ‘shell and core’ floor space at ground floor for use by the Council
•             A bus apron area to include at least 5 bus stands and bus movement area
•             Enhanced public realm

contracts.title: Funding of additional affordable rented accommodation in West Lancashire
contracts.description:
West Lancashire Borough Council is keen to increase the supply of affordable housing in the Borough, and is seeking to establish the potential interest from the market in the provision of public or private funding to support the delivery of additional affordable rented accommodation.
The Council currently retains capital receipts from Council properties which are sold through Right to Buy arrangements. Retained capital receipts must be used to increase the supply of affordable rented housing. This may occur through new build or acquisitions of existing property, however, no more than 30% of the retained capital receipt can be applied to each unit / overall development costs.   
The Council is therefore interested in securing public or private funding from organisations to develop affordable housing with the organisation providing the required 70% funding.
